title: Yellow Spicy Chinese Pork Dumplings
description: A traditional Chinese dish featuring minced garlic and a spicy kick, these dumplings are perfect for a special occasion, with a chewy texture and a flavor that is both mustardy and slightly sweet from the tempering chocolate, and are fodmap friendly.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground pork, minced garlic, grated ginger, mustard, salt, and black pepper, and mix well until just combined.
Melt the tempering chocolate in a double boiler or in the microwave in 10 second increments, stirring between each interval until smooth.
Add the melted chocolate to the pork mixture and mix until just combined.
Lay a dumpling wrapper on a flat surface and place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of sesame oil and run it along the edge of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point, and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
In a large pot, bring a quart of water to a boil and add the dumplings, being careful not to overcrowd the pot.
Cook the dumplings for 10-12 minutes, or until they float to the surface.
Remove the dumplings from the pot with a slotted spoon and serve immediately.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F and let it rest for 3 minutes before serving.
